about: Test sheets for Lantern's Sheet Music Reader (1.21.0), engraved with Verovio 6.4 from the ABC and Humdrum below and rasterised in Chromium at 1300, 900 and 700 pixels wide (staff lines about 11, 7 and 5.5 pixels apart). Tunes: public domain (Beethoven's Ode to Joy, Twinkle Twinkle, Frere Jacques) or written for these tests; all CC0. bars: each bar's notes as [midi or null for a rest, length in quarter notes]. 1.21.1: the piano sheets' chords (from the left hand) and ode_title_900.png's heading (the same Ode with its title and composer printed above). 1.21.2: three at screenshot sizes (ode_c_820, minor_a_760 and twinkle_g_760: staff lines about 6.5 and 6 pixels apart; beams, sharps and whole notes, notes close to bar lines, a staff with no time signature). 1.22.1: ode_banner_900.png, the piano Ode with a dark banner across its second left hand (a web page's preview): the banner left out and said, the tune read, the chords of the covered bars chosen by Lantern. Remake with make_sheets.py (needs verovio and playwright). 1.22.4: minor_e_piano_900.png and _760.png, a piece written for these tests (E minor, a grand staff): eighth rests and beamed sixteenths, whole-note chords in the left hand, a chord whose sharp a tie runs into (D to D#dim), a sharpened chord tied over the bar line (B, its D# carried), an end-repeat bar line; the key E minor from the left hand, the chords as the left hand plays them (with the tune's B and A over its D#-F#-A and B-D#-F#, B7). 1.22.5: voice_e_piano_900.png, a song written for these tests (E major): a voice with its words over a piano, the three staves of each line joined at their left end -- the tune is the voice's, and in the two bars where the voice rests (the piano's introduction), the right hand's top notes; the left hand gives the chords. 1.22.6: ode_clarinet.pdf, the Ode as a clarinet part in B flat (printed in D major) made into a PDF by Chromium from Verovio's drawing, with its title and instrument printed above: no picture in it -- Lantern draws the page, reads it as music, and gives the tune as it sounds (C major). 1.22.7: barcarolle_g_piano_900.png, a piece written for these tests in G minor and 12/8 (as Adam's sheet, a published arrangement kept out): the left hand a quarter and an eighth four times a bar, the right hand dotted quarters and eighths beamed in threes (beams below the staff) -- the time read from the digits printed after the key, not guessed from the bars; jig_d_900.png and _760.png, a 6/8 tune engraved in Leland (MuseScore 4's music font), its 6 curled shut on itself. 1.22.8: ode_viewer.png, the piano Ode as a PDF viewer shows it (Adam's screenshot): the sheet on a white page, the page on dark grey -- the page cut out and read. 1.23.1: piano_b_lyrics_900.png -- a piano piece written for these tests in B major (piano_b_musicxml, MusicXML), with the things Adam's piano page had that the reader misread: words under the right hand (their hyphens were read as rests), an octave sign's dotted line under the left hand, chords tied an eighth into a sixteenth and a quarter into an eighth (held, not struck again: ties), dotted rhythms, a bar of high notes with their stems down and the beams inside the staff (taken out with the lines), a sixteenth rest, a dotted eighth rest, a lone sixteenth's two flags, and a left hand of quarters over whole notes (two voices).
